title: School Construction Committee
before:
School Construction Committee

The School Construction Committee of the Maine State Board of Education is charged with conducting the Board's business related to its school construction responsibilities. The State Board of Education is required by Maine law to adopt standards governing school construction and to approve all Major Capital School Construction projects for receipt of state funds.

Membership
  • Fern Desjardins, Chair
  • Edmond Morin
  • Paulette Bonneau

Meeting Information

Unless otherwise noted, meetings are held at 9:00 AM in Room 500 of the Cross State Office Building in Augusta. All meetings are open to the public.

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Give the cards the width their content needs
decisions.why: 1 row holds two cards of very different weight in equal halves, and cards in a row are the same height — so the short one is stretched and the difference shows as empty space. 29.2× — 1842 characters beside 63. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Say what it is before who is on it
decisions.why: This page opens with a narrow card listing the members, and only to the right of it says what the committee does and when it meets. A roster answers a question the reader does not have yet — and because columns stack in source order, on a phone the names are the whole first screen. The two columns swap; no words move and neither column changes width.

decisions.label: Remove the first section header
decisions.why: "School Construction Committee" repeats the page title, so the reader is told the same thing twice before any content.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: The School Construction Committee of the Maine State Board of Education is charged with conducting the Board's business related to its school construction responsibilities. The State Board of Education is required by Maine law to adopt standards governing school construction and to approve all Major Capital School Construction projects for receipt of state funds.

decisions.label: Bring every heading up to h3 or above
decisions.why: 1 heading sat at h4 or deeper inside a card, a callout, a contact block or an accordion panel — components the outline walk leaves alone because they label a thing rather than a section. A reader using a screen reader still hears the level, so a fourth-level title inside a page that only goes to three is announced as belonging to a level that does not exist. Each is styled by its class and its position rather than its number, so nothing changes on screen.

decisions.label: Let a long table be searched
decisions.why: 1 table runs to fifteen rows or more, so finding one row means reading every row. The theme already loads the search behaviour on every page and switches it on for any table marked this way — 26 tables across the site already are, including the contact directory. It adds a search box and a "show 25 entries" menu above the table, makes the column headings sortable, and pages below twenty-five rows at a time — which leaves all but the longest tables whole. Nothing is reordered and nothing changes until someone types.
